title: Mavrone,
html_source:
mavrone
Interjection
An expression of sorrow; alas.
Origin
Anglo-Irish, from Irish mo bhrón, from mo (“my”) + brón (“grief”).

anchor.prefix:
, I'm thinking, and he limp with leching. And we one hour and two hours and three hours in Connery's sitting civil waiting for pints apiece. 

 He wailed: 

 — And we to be there,
anchor.suffix:
and you to be unbeknownst sending us your conglomerations the way we to have our tongues out a yard long like the drouthy clerics do be fainting for a pussful. 

 Stephen laughed.
